epic.title: crew-verdict-and-door
epic.intent_and_why: Stop scripts/run_crew.py from reporting failed for a crew whose successful archive relocated the result artifact it was told to watch, while never letting a genuinely failed crew read as completed; secondarily, harden the external backend's already-known unbound-MCP-door hazard.

definition_of_done: A dispatch given both --spine and --result, whose result is missing/stale and whose bound spine is terminal, reads completed (was failed).
A dispatch with a non-terminal spine and no result still reads failed.
blocked_gate still wins ahead of both other paths, unchanged.
external-backend dispatch states plainly, in the registry entry and at dispatch time, that its door is unbound.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: TDD red-before-green on the real finalize_from_exit_code, cache-clean full suite green
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Independent reviewer re-reproduces every claimed test result rather than trusting pasted output
good_enough.appetite: One bounded fix plus one bounded hardening, both in scripts/run_crew.py

hard_constraints: Yours: scripts/run_crew.py and its tests only
Must not make a genuinely failed crew read as completed
Do not attempt to bind the external backend's door out-of-band -- impossible by construction
fixed_decisions: task-1-is-the-lane: ship Task 1 even if Task 2 is deferred
no-admiral-side-workarounds: the fix lives in the launcher, not in doctrine handed to every Admiral

current_wave.objective: Fix the inverted archive verdict and harden the unbound external-door hazard, both in scripts/run_crew.py
exit_criteria: g1 (verdict fix) closes with reviewer APPROVE and a cache-clean green suite
g2 (door hardening) closes with reviewer APPROVE and a cache-clean green suite, or is deferred with a named reason if it needs a design decision

issues.title: Stop the inverted archive verdict
issues.desired_outcome: finalize_from_exit_code falls back to spine_terminal when the result artifact is missing/stale, following the blocked_gate-checked-first precedent.
issues.useful_now: Every successful archive currently reports failed, which risks an Admiral relaunching a Commander onto already-archived work with the duplicate-guard disarmed.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: test_finalize_terminal_spine_rescues_missing_result (red before, green after), test_finalize_still_fails_when_spine_not_terminal, test_finalize_blocked_wins_regardless_of_result_or_spine, all calling finalize_from_exit_code directly.
issues.implementation_latitude: Choose the exact verdict_source field's internal branching; the fix's shape (spine_terminal fallback, blocked_gate-first precedent) is pinned by the launch order.
hard_constraints_no_gos: Must not touch result_exists, result_fresh, spine_terminal, or spine_blocked_id
local_unknowns: Whether any gate other than archive relocates artifacts the launcher watches
Whether a failed verdict should ever be recordable while the bound spine is terminal

issues.title: Harden the unbound external-backend door
issues.desired_outcome: Every external-backend registry entry and every external dispatch states plainly that its MCP door is unbound.
issues.useful_now: A claim through a demo-bound door mutates the wrong spine while reporting success -- this already happened during epic 568.
issues.implementation_latitude: Choose the exact banner wording; the two-piece scope (registry field + stderr banner) is pinned by the corrected handoff.
hard_constraints_no_gos: Do not attempt to bind the door out-of-band

wave_forecast.outcome: recover_crews.py surfaces door_bound in its human-facing report
wave_forecast.why_likely: The reviewer flagged it as a natural next step now that the field exists on every entry
entry_conditions: a triage candidate is filed and picked up

parked_possibilities: A dispatch-time-aware spine_terminal (or a caller-side staleness guard mirroring result_fresh), so a leftover terminal spine from an earlier attempt cannot rescue a later attempt's stale result

completed_outcomes.outcome: finalize_from_exit_code rescues a missing/stale result into completed when the bound spine is terminal; a genuine failure still reads failed; blocked_gate still wins first.
completed_outcomes.evidence: Reviewer APPROVE (e-g1-review-1); cache-clean, env-clean full suite 3009 passed/6 skipped/0 failed/1130 subtests after both gates; red-before-green independently reproduced by the Commander via git stash on the unfixed function.

completed_outcomes.outcome: build_entry records entry["door_bound"] on every registry entry (True only for the cli backend); ExternalBackend.dispatch prints an unconditional stderr banner naming the unbound door -- independently observed firing live on this run's own g2-reviewer dispatch.
completed_outcomes.evidence: Reviewer APPROVE (e-g2-review-1); same cache-clean green suite; Fowler pass 11/12 absent, one non-blocking string-level duplication noted.

A cold plan critic caught this before dispatch.
discrepancies.evidence: Cold plan critic finding (HIGH severity), verified by direct re-read of ExternalBackend.dispatch's own docstring/comments before the plan was frozen
discrepancies.reason: Repair is evidence-led: the plan's anchors and imperative were corrected (to the registry-entry field + stderr banner, both genuinely inside scripts/run_crew.py) before g2 was dispatched, not after a failed attempt.

discrepancies.affects: How this Commander (and any future spine-bound Commander) must run the full suite for a clean baseline
discrepancies.evidence: The test passes when run with `env -u SPINE_FILE -u SPINE_SESSION -u SPINE_PARENT`; fails identically, with the same assertion, when run in this shell as-is
discrepancies.reason: No issue is warranted; the execute.json suite-check commands were amended (via the engine's retext-check verb, authority=commander) to strip those three vars, which is a run-local mechanical fix, not a doctrine change.

discrepancies.reason: No issue is warranted from this run's latitude; likely a pre-existing conditional skip unrelated to this diff, recorded rather than silently absorbed into the pass-count comparison.
